Generate an augmented row-column field design

Source: R/augmented_row_column.R
augmented_row_column_design.Rd

Randomizes unreplicated treatments and replicated controls (checks) in an augmented row-column design with superimposed blocks (Piepho and Williams, 2016). Adjacent rows form row groups and adjacent columns form column groups; each intersection is a block that receives a given number of check plots. Row, column and block effects are all estimable from the checks, and the layout must leave positive error degrees of freedom (see augmented_row_column_capacity()).

Usage

augmented_row_column_design(
  treatments,
  controls,
  rows_in_field = NULL,
  cols_in_field = NULL,
  rows_per_block = NULL,
  cols_per_block = NULL,
  plot_type = c("serpentine", "cartesian"),
  n_candidates = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  output_file = NULL,
  rows_per_rowgroup = NULL,
  cols_per_colgroup = NULL,
  checks_per_block = NULL,
  method = c("auto", "latin", "optimal")
)

Arguments

treatments

Character vector of unreplicated treatment/entry names. Its length must equal the number of entry plots.

controls

Character vector of replicated check/control names.

rows_in_field

Number of rows in the whole field.

cols_in_field

Number of columns in the whole field.

rows_per_block

Number of rows in each row group (equal groups).

cols_per_block

Number of columns in each column group (equal groups).

plot_type

Plot numbering order. Use "serpentine" or "cartesian".

n_candidates

Number of candidate layouts ("latin") or random restarts of the local search ("optimal", at most 50; the search stops after 3 restarts without improvement).

seed

Optional random seed.

output_file

Optional path for writing the complete design as a tab-delimited file.

rows_per_rowgroup, cols_per_colgroup

Optional vectors of unequal group sizes, as in augmented_row_column_capacity().

checks_per_block

Optional number of check plots per block, as in augmented_row_column_capacity().

method

Check allocation method: "auto", "latin" or "optimal".

Value

A list with:

input

Validated design inputs.

summary

Design size, error df, method, and the D-criterion d_criterion (det(X'X)^(1/p) of the check-plot model; higher is better), and the number of pairs of neighbouring check plots (same column in consecutive rows, or same row in consecutive columns) inside a block and across block boundaries.

design

Complete plot-level design with row, column, block, entry, control flag, and plot order.

breedbase_design

Breedbase-compatible columns: plots, block, all_entries, rep, and is_control.

Details

Two check-allocation methods are available:

"latin"

For equal groups where every block is a complete block of checks (one copy of each). Checks are placed with covering Latin rectangles, so controls never share a row or column within a block, the same control never appears twice in a field row or column, and every field row and column has a check. Candidates are scored for spatial spread and row/column balance.

"optimal"

The general strategy of Piepho and Williams (2016): unequal group sizes and any number of check plots per block (incomplete blocks or extra replication of checks). Check labels are first allocated to blocks balancing row groups, column groups and blocks (Step 2); check plots are then placed within blocks and the layout improved by a local search that maximizes the D-criterion of the check-plot model row + column + rowgroup:colgroup + check (Steps 3-5). Check plots next to each other (same column in consecutive rows, or same row in consecutive columns) are avoided, inside blocks above all, and spatial spread breaks ties. Entries fill the remaining plots at random (Step 6).

method = "auto" uses "latin" when it applies and "optimal" otherwise.

References

Piepho, H.-P. and Williams, E. R. (2016). Augmented row-column designs for a small number of checks. Agronomy Journal 108, 2256-2262. doi:10.2134/agronj2016.06.0325

Examples

treatments <- paste0("G", seq_len(108))
controls <- paste0("Check", seq_len(4))

design <- augmented_row_column_design(
  treatments = treatments,
  controls = controls,
  rows_in_field = 12,
  cols_in_field = 12,
  rows_per_block = 4,
  cols_per_block = 4,
  n_candidates = 50,
  seed = 123
)

head(design$design)
#>   plots row col block rowgroup colgroup all_entries  type rep is_control
#> 1     1   1   1     1        1        1         G16 entry   1          0
#> 2     2   1   2     1        1        1         G74 entry   1          0
#> 3     3   1   3     1        1        1         G63 entry   1          0
#> 4     4   1   4     1        1        1      Check3 check   1          1
#> 5     5   1   5     2        1        2         G88 entry   1          0
#> 6     6   1   6     2        1        2         G44 entry   1          0
design$summary
#> # A tibble: 1 × 25
#>   rows_in_field cols_in_field rows_per_block cols_per_block n_block_rows
#>           <int>         <int>          <int>          <int>        <int>
#> 1            12            12              4              4            3
#> # ℹ 20 more variables: n_block_cols <int>, n_blocks <int>, n_controls <int>,
#> #   total_plots <int>, check_plots <int>, entry_plots <int>, error_df <dbl>,
#> #   check_fraction <dbl>, min_rowgroup_slack <dbl>, min_colgroup_slack <dbl>,
#> #   every_row_has_check <lgl>, every_col_has_check <lgl>, method <chr>,
#> #   plot_type <chr>, n_candidates <int>, n_valid_candidates <int>,
#> #   design_score <dbl>, d_criterion <dbl>, adjacent_checks_in_blocks <int>,
#> #   adjacent_checks_across_blocks <int>

# Example 3 of Piepho and Williams (2016): 173 entries, 4 checks, unequal
# row and column groups, and 3 to 5 check plots per block.
pb <- rbind(c(4, 5, 4), c(3, 5, 3), c(3, 5, 4), c(3, 5, 3))
ex3 <- augmented_row_column_design(
  treatments = paste0("E", 1:173),
  controls = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
  rows_per_rowgroup = c(6, 5, 6, 5),
  cols_per_colgroup = c(3, 4, 3),
  checks_per_block = pb,
  n_candidates = 3,
  seed = 1
)
ex3$summary[, c("method", "check_plots", "entry_plots", "error_df", "d_criterion")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   method  check_plots entry_plots error_df d_criterion
#>   <chr>         <int>       <int>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 optimal          47         173        7        1.94
